save_note: 1000 rows / 16 = 63 steps per epoch, 378 steps in total; a checkpoint every 2 epochs (steps 126, 252, 378). Measured on G4 in the smoke: a local save is 113.5 GiB in 386 s, and the local disk holds one checkpoint at a time. Google Drive accepts about 750 GiB of uploads per 24 hours, so saving every epoch (5 mirrors, ~610 GiB per run) would allow one run per day; every 2 epochs is 2 mirrors + the 14 GiB export, ~241 GiB per run, at the cost of losing up to 126 steps if the VM disappears. Saving does not change the training math.
recipe_note: QFFT official yaml (LLaMA-Factory examples/train_qfft/train_s1_qfft.yaml): full FT, LR 1e-5, 6 epochs, cosine, warmup_ratio 0.1, wd 1e-4, default AdamW betas (0.9, 0.999), 16K cutoff with truncation, batch 8 (8 GPUs, ZeRO-3 offload). v93 keeps every optimizer setting and changes two things: batch 16 (as s1.1-7B) to halve CPU-Adam steps, and a 32K window without truncation so all 1000 traces end with their answer.
